correctness.rationale: The fair-refresh clock yields actual spin flips at a/2, so its contribution to the linear spin drift is -a, not -2a. At positive a the finite chain is irreducible and reversal symmetry centers M. An independent spectral reconstruction uses the symmetric neighbor matrix P and J=(1+a)I+P. The spin drift is -J; for the stationary correlation matrix C the off-diagonal entries of JC+CJ are zero because no jump changes two sites. Transitivity makes the diagonal scalar, so positivity of J and C_ii=1 give C=J^(-1)/d, where d=tr(J^(-1))/(rn). The eigenvalues of P are 1, -1/(r-1), 0 with multiplicities 1, r-1, r(n-1); the weights of M form an eigenvector at the second eigenvalue and have squared norm 2/n. This gives Var(M)=2/(n*d*lambda), with lambda=a+(r-2)/(r-1); reducing this expression gives the frozen rational formula. The semigroup on M alone has decay exp(-lambda*t), proving both covariance and integration without any statement about the full chain gap. At a=c/n the denominator is 1+2c+c²/n for r=2 and 2(r-2)n+O(1) otherwise, and lambda is c/n versus a positive constant. These yield the two time scales and all four limiting amplitudes. An exact independent rational occupancy-chain check (not the supplied spin-level script) confirmed the variance and generator equation in three finite examples, including r=4. Susceptibility here is defined as integrated stationary covariance, not a general response-to-field identity.
residual_risks: Stationarity uses a>0 first; the limits fix c and r and do not claim an a=0 stationary choice or a process-level limit.

evidence: Kitching et al. allow pure unfaithful copying at the transition-rate level (set the faithful rates to zero and give the two signs equal unfaithful and spontaneous rates). The anti-voter parameter choice maps to a negative noise-to-order ratio, so the scope of any positive-ratio interpretation is not taken for granted.

Carro et al. give faithful-copy dynamics and an annealed approximation for the stationary amplitude; their equations (4)–(5) are general moment machinery. Gantert et al. cover qualitative ergodicity and frustration of signed systems without the present finite refreshing contrast comparison.

value.rationale: An opposed shore magnetization is natural for the unfrustrated anti-voter dynamics, and adding a third shore is the canonical first frustrated complete multipartite case. At identical per-shore size and refresh parameter, the corresponding integrated fluctuation scales differ by order n². The explicit amplitudes and lag limits quantify the distinction without annealed-network approximations, and the exact positive-refresh contrast law is a useful finite-graph benchmark. The value is the quantitative frustrated comparison, not the elementary exponential integration in isolation.
residual_risks: Only contrast on balanced, completely negative complete multipartite graphs. The term threshold does not assert a thermodynamic transition of the whole chain.
